description_full: MasterCraft Boat Holdings, Inc., through its subsidiaries, designs, manufactures, and markets recreational powerboats. It operates through Performance and Wake, Leisure, and Recreation and Sport Fishing segments. The Performance and Wake Segment manufactures and sells ski/wake boats used for water skiing, wakeboarding, wake surfing, and general recreational boating under the MasterCraft brand name. The Leisure segment manufactures and sells pontoon boats used for general recreational boating under the Crest and Balise brand names. Recreation and Sport Fishing Segment provides manufactures and sells recreational fiberglass powerboats for both the pleasure boating and sport fishing markets under the Chaparral and Robalo brand names. It also provides trailers, marine parts, aftermarket parts, and accessories. The company sells products through a network of independent dealers in the United States and internationally. The company was formerly known as MCBC Holdings, Inc. and changed its name to MasterCraft Boat Holdings, Inc. in November 2018. MasterCraft Boat Holdings, Inc. was founded in 1968 and is headquartered in Vonore, Tennessee.

financial_summary: MasterCraft Boat Holdings, Inc. is a small-cap consumer cyclical business with a $493M market cap on $349M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -19% over the past three years and +5% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.

Returns on capital run at 5% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 24% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.
The business throws off $22M in free cash flow — roughly 6 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin -5.2× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 0.5%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 25% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.0× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
